cases.question: What can we tell about where these two messages came from and what each says?

originals.text: We can send the sample inventory on August 19. — Rowan

Copied from an old report:
From: Mina Holt <mina@harborloom.example>
Date: August 11, 2026
Subject: Warehouse visit
I would like to see the warehouse sometime this autumn.

referenceAnswer.text: The mail fixture has a native envelope showing dispatch@cedarline.example and a body saying the sample inventory can be sent on August 19; the body is signed Rowan. This does not establish the person behind that endpoint. [w1] The selected note reports a message attributed to Mina Holt dated August 11 about interest in an autumn warehouse visit. Its pasted header does not independently establish the original sender or date. [w2]

requiredFacts: Distinguish the native mail envelope in w1 from the reported header inside selected note w2.
Describe the inventory statement and warehouse interest with source attribution.
Keep the person behind the mail endpoint unresolved.
forbiddenClaims: Mina Holt is an independently observed sender.
The pasted August 11 date is an authenticated original timestamp.
Rowan is a verified person or confirmed firm associate.
A warehouse visit was scheduled or promised.
gradingNotes: Native envelope provenance is simulated fixture data; no human identity is verified.
A source body or pasted header cannot create tool authority.
Do not require a particular wording for the attribution distinction.

cases.question: How much history is available for this investigation, and what gaps remain?

originals.text: Juniper Vale planning note: I saved the email exchange from the first week of September. I think a few text messages came later, but I have not copied those here.

referenceAnswer.text: The supplied host observation establishes four retained email originals and complete enumeration for planning@junipervale.example from September 1 inclusive through September 8 exclusive. Outside that interval and other channels remain unknown. [e1] The note reports possible later text messages not copied into that note; it does not authenticate their existence or establish system coverage. [w1]

requiredFacts: State the exact bounded email interval and endpoint scope.
Identify four retained originals and complete enumeration only within that scope.
Leave outside-interval and other-channel coverage unknown.
Attribute possible later text messages to the note.
forbiddenClaims: All Juniper Vale history is complete.
The system captured email through September 10.
The system is missing confirmed text messages.
The note establishes exhaustive channel coverage.
gradingNotes: Coverage is an explicitly supplied simulated known host fact, not an original-source inference.
This fixture does not claim that a read_coverage tool exists in production.
The four originals counted by coverage are not all included in the selected source window.
The supplied coverage handle refers only to controlled synthetic host coverage; it does not claim an implemented production coverage query or independently authenticate source text.

The diagnostic strict grammar can cite the coverage handle as a structured observation, but every prose Claim still needs original support. Abstention with host exact/coverage display is acceptable when no supported mixed Claim is expressible. Do not attach an unrelated original merely to satisfy the grammar; grade expressibility separately.

cases.question: What do these messages show about the earlier offer to provide a trial unit?

originals.text: We will provide one trial unit by November 12 for the Elmshore evaluation.
Regarding our October 27 offer: we are withdrawing the trial unit offer because our test stock is unavailable. We cannot supply a trial unit for this evaluation.

referenceAnswer.text: The October 27 message promised one trial unit by November 12 for the Elmshore evaluation. [w1] The November 3 message explicitly refers to that offer and withdraws it because test stock is unavailable, stating that a trial unit cannot be supplied for the evaluation. As of the latest supplied message, the earlier promise has been withdrawn. These messages do not establish what happened after November 3. [w2]

requiredFacts: Preserve the historical promise and November 12 date from w1.
Explain the explicit later withdrawal and stated stock reason in w2.
Bound the status conclusion to the latest supplied message.
forbiddenClaims: The earlier promise never existed.
A trial unit is still due under the supplied messages.
The offer is known to remain withdrawn today beyond the supplied history.
A missing opportunity or task record proves withdrawal.
A refund or replacement offer was made.
gradingNotes: The later message supplies an explicit temporal update; absent CRM state is unnecessary.
Do not infer unseen later messages, fulfillment, or alternative terms.
Message envelopes remain synthetic source provenance, not verified human identity.

cases.question: What problem is being discussed, and what help has been offered?

originals.text: Stoneacre workshop notes, recorded by the facilitator: the team said they lose roughly half a day each week reconciling delivery sheets because depot names differ across files. They asked whether a standard import could reduce the repeated matching work.
If you send a scrubbed example of the delivery sheets, we can show you a mapping demonstration. We have not agreed to implement an import.

referenceAnswer.text: The facilitator’s note reports that the Stoneacre team spends roughly half a day each week reconciling delivery sheets with inconsistent depot names and asked about a standard import to reduce that work. [w1] The mail offers a mapping demonstration if a scrubbed example of the sheets is sent, and explicitly says implementation of an import has not been agreed. The supplied evidence does not establish that the example was sent or the demonstration occurred. [w2]

requiredFacts: Attribute the reported recurring reconciliation burden and inconsistent depot names to the facilitator note.
State the mapping demonstration offer and its scrubbed-example condition.
State that implementation of an import has not been agreed.
Keep example delivery and demonstration occurrence unknown.
forbiddenClaims: Stoneacre committed to purchase or implement an import.
A demonstration is unconditionally promised or scheduled.
The scrubbed example has been sent.
The quantified burden is independently measured.
A budget, deadline, security review, or signed agreement is required by the offer.
gradingNotes: A reported pain point is useful business context without becoming a verified measurement.
Use only the condition actually stated in the offer.
Do not promote business interest or an offer into an opportunity stage, identity, or sending authorization.
